mascot: Officer Mark — a friendly traffic officer with a magnifying glass and a big badge shaped like a full stop.

slides.title: Little Marks, Big Job! ✍️
slides.text: Punctuation marks are little signs that help readers! They show when to stop, when to ask, and when to shout!
slides.spoken: Punctuation marks show when to stop, ask or shout!

slides.title: The Full Stop (.) 🔴
slides.text: The full stop ends a telling sentence. "The sun is hot." When you read and see a full stop — stop and take a breath!
slides.spoken: The full stop ends a telling sentence. Stop and take a breath!

slides.title: The Question Mark (?) ❓
slides.text: The question mark ends an asking sentence. "Where is my bag?" When you see it, your voice goes up!
slides.spoken: The question mark ends an asking sentence!

slides.title: The Exclamation Mark (!) 🎉
slides.text: The exclamation mark shows big feelings! "What a lovely day!" "Watch out!" It means wow, hurray or careful!
slides.spoken: The exclamation mark shows big feelings: wow, hurray, careful!

slides.title: Capital Letters and the Comma (,) 📝
slides.text: Sentences need capital letters at the start, and names like Ravi get one too! The comma (,) makes a tiny pause in lists: apples, mangoes and bananas.
slides.spoken: Capitals start sentences and names. The comma makes a tiny pause!

challenges.question: Which mark ends a question?
challenges.hint: When we ask something, the little hook mark goes at the end!
challenges.misconception: A question ends with a question mark (?) — 'Where is my bag?'

challenges.question: Which mark ends a strong happy sentence like 'What a lovely day'?
challenges.hint: For big wow feelings, we need the excited mark!
challenges.misconception: Big feelings get an exclamation mark (!) — 'What a lovely day!'

challenges.question: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
challenges.hint: The sentence starts with a capital AND the name needs one too!
challenges.misconception: 'My name is Ravi.' is correct: a capital at the start and a capital R for the name Ravi!

challenges.question: Which mark finishes this question: 'Where is my school bag'?
challenges.hint: This sentence asks for something — which mark does a question need?
challenges.misconception: 'Where is my school bag?' is a question, so it needs a question mark!

challenges.question: In 'i love mangoes.', which word needs a capital letter?
challenges.hint: One tiny word must ALWAYS be a capital, every single time!
challenges.misconception: The word 'i' must always be capital: 'I love mangoes.' — the letter I stands tall!

challenges.question: Drag each sentence! Does it need a question mark or a full stop?
challenges.hint: 'Where is my cap' asks. 'The cap is red' tells!
challenges.misconception: Asking sentences like 'Where is my cap' need a question mark. Telling sentences like 'The cap is red' need a full stop!

challenges.question: Which sentence is complete and correct?
challenges.answer: The sun rises in the east.
options: the sun rises in the east
The sun rises in the east
The sun rises in the east.
challenges.hint: It needs a capital at the start AND a full stop at the end!
challenges.misconception: 'The sun rises in the east.' is complete: capital T and a full stop at the end!

options: The sun rises in the east.
The sun rises in the east

challenges.question: Which mark makes a tiny pause inside a list, like 'apples, mangoes and bananas'?
challenges.hint: The tiniest mark of all makes a tiny pause between list items!
challenges.misconception: The comma (,) makes the tiny pause in lists: apples, mangoes and bananas.
